questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute limit of detection from blank statistics
questions.stem: A blank has standard deviation 0.0174 signal units and the calibration slope is 2.924 signal per concentration unit. What is the limit of detection, using the 3-sigma convention?

options.misconception: uses one sigma rather than three
uses the ten-sigma limit of quantitation instead of detection
multiplies by slope instead of dividing

questions.explanation: The detection limit is three times the blank standard deviation divided by the calibration slope, converting a signal threshold into concentration. The quantitation limit uses ten sigma, and multiplying by slope would not produce a concentration.

questions.stem: In the routine spectrophotometric assay exercise below, a researcher obtains the reported result. Which figure of merit describes the ability of a method to measure the analyte correctly in the presence of potential interferents?

options.text: Specificity, which is the capacity to respond only to the intended analyte
The limit of detection, which is the smallest measurable signal
options.misconception: mistakes a detection threshold for selectivity

options.text: Linearity, which describes how well response scales with concentration
options.misconception: confuses calibration linearity with interference resistance

options.text: Precision, which describes agreement among replicates
options.misconception: confuses repeatability with selectivity

questions.explanation: Specificity is the extent to which a method responds only to the analyte of interest despite other species being present. Linearity, precision, and detection limit describe calibration shape, repeatability, and sensitivity respectively, not freedom from interference.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute limit of detection from blank statistics
questions.stem: A blank has standard deviation 0.0324 signal units and the calibration slope is 3.905 signal per concentration unit. What is the limit of detection, using the 3-sigma convention?

options.misconception: uses one sigma rather than three
multiplies by slope instead of dividing
uses the ten-sigma limit of quantitation instead of detection

questions.explanation: The detection limit is three times the blank standard deviation divided by the calibration slope, converting a signal threshold into concentration. The quantitation limit uses ten sigma, and multiplying by slope would not produce a concentration.

questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: compute limit of detection from blank statistics
questions.stem: A blank has standard deviation 0.0305 signal units and the calibration slope is 0.947 signal per concentration unit. Calculate the limit of detection, using the 3-sigma convention?

options.misconception: uses the ten-sigma limit of quantitation instead of detection
multiplies by slope instead of dividing
uses one sigma rather than three

questions.explanation: The detection limit is three times the blank standard deviation divided by the calibration slope, converting a signal threshold into concentration. The quantitation limit uses ten sigma, and multiplying by slope would not produce a concentration.
